name: no-op rule
rule: A text is a no-op only when NO_OP_RE matches it and it asks Jack nothing real.

Remove every URL_RE and NO_OP_RE match, then every GENERIC_ASK_RE match: a sentence or clause that is entirely a generic ask ('What next?', 'What should happen next?', 'Anything else?'), starting at the text start or right after . ; : ! or ?. A generic word inside a real question ('ship now or what?', 'For prod, what should we do next?') is never removed. Then look at what is left.
If ASK_LEFT_RE still matches what is left (a '?', an 'Options:' list or a 'Rec:' line), the text is a real ask and never a no-op, even when the ask shares a sentence with the phrase.
has_real_question means another question of the same item is real. Then a text whose NO_OP_RE matches all start with 'nothing else' is not a no-op either.
no_op_re: \bnothing (?:here |else )?(?:needs?|for) (?:jack|you)\b|\bnothing (?:to (?:fix|do|decide)|needs? (?:fixing|doing))\b|\bno (?:decision|action|input) (?:is )?(?:needed|required|for jack)\b|\bnot (?:a decision|an action item) for jack\b
generic_ask_re: (?:^|(?<=[.;:!?]))\s*\b(?:what(?: should (?:happen|we do)| do we do| now)?(?: next)?|anything else)\s*\?
